final_answer:
Yes, two pairs of CAPAs appear to share an upstream cause. The stronger one is the FRZ-80-02 freezer failure. The weaker one is the INC-03 door-alarm fault.

**Strongest link: CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016 share the FRZ-80-02 freezer excursion**

- **CAPA-26-008** comes from DEV-26-021. The recorded root cause is an age-related compressor failure. FRZ-80-02 alarmed on 20 Apr 2026 with the compressor not running and reached about −36 °C before relocation. The vector lot LV25-118 was in that freezer.
- **CAPA-26-016** comes from DEV-26-027. The recorded root cause is suspected donor variability (low CD3%). The deviation covers ENG26-01 and ENG26-02, which had FC-CAR of 19.8% and 11.9% against a 20% target.
- **Why the freezer is the shared cause:**
  - ENG26-01, ENG26-02 and ENG26-03 all used vector lot LV25-118, which is the lot that was in FRZ-80-02 during the excursion. ENG26-03 is not linked to DEV-26-027 but shows the same low result (FC-CAR 13.9%).
  - Lot LV25-118 gave normal results before the excursion: PD26-014, PD26-015 and PD26-016 (March 2026) had FC-CAR of 34.5–36.4%.
  - The donor explanation does not fit. ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 had CD3% of 65.3 and 63.8, which is not low, and FC-CD3 was 96% and 96%.
  - Later runs on other vector lots (LV26-007, LV26-021) gave FC-CAR of 37–39%.
  - Caveat: the CoA titre (104 TU/mL) is from before the excursion, and no post-excursion titre is in the data. The potency loss is inferred from the pattern, not measured. Also, pd.material_lot still records LV25-118 at FRZ-80-02, even though DEV-26-021 says the contents were relocated to FRZ-80-01. That record needs checking.

**Weaker link: CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015 share the INC-03 door-alarm fault**

- **CAPA-26-012** comes from DEV-26-011. The recorded root cause is a misaligned INC-03 door switch, and the OQ door-open alarm took 142 s against a 60 s limit.
- **CAPA-26-015** comes from DEV-26-033. The recorded root cause is that the operator did not confirm the door latch, which is human error. INC-03's door was found not fully latched during PPQ26-02, and the door alarm was acknowledged about 10 hours after it started (21:40 to 07:50).
- Both events involve INC-03's door and alarm chain. The PPQ CAPA addresses only operator retraining, not the door-switch defect that CAPA-26-012 is meant to fix. I would treat this as a likely contributing cause rather than a proven one.

The other CAPA, CAPA-26-019 (DEV-26-041), is an independent supplier tubing defect and does not share a cause with the others.

content.text:
Yes, two pairs of CAPAs appear to share an upstream cause. The stronger one is the FRZ-80-02 freezer failure. The weaker one is the INC-03 door-alarm fault.

**Strongest link: CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016 share the FRZ-80-02 freezer excursion**

- **CAPA-26-008** comes from DEV-26-021. The recorded root cause is an age-related compressor failure. FRZ-80-02 alarmed on 20 Apr 2026 with the compressor not running and reached about −36 °C before relocation. The vector lot LV25-118 was in that freezer.
- **CAPA-26-016** comes from DEV-26-027. The recorded root cause is suspected donor variability (low CD3%). The deviation covers ENG26-01 and ENG26-02, which had FC-CAR of 19.8% and 11.9% against a 20% target.
- **Why the freezer is the shared cause:**
  - ENG26-01, ENG26-02 and ENG26-03 all used vector lot LV25-118, which is the lot that was in FRZ-80-02 during the excursion. ENG26-03 is not linked to DEV-26-027 but shows the same low result (FC-CAR 13.9%).
  - Lot LV25-118 gave normal results before the excursion: PD26-014, PD26-015 and PD26-016 (March 2026) had FC-CAR of 34.5–36.4%.
  - The donor explanation does not fit. ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 had CD3% of 65.3 and 63.8, which is not low, and FC-CD3 was 96% and 96%.
  - Later runs on other vector lots (LV26-007, LV26-021) gave FC-CAR of 37–39%.
  - Caveat: the CoA titre (104 TU/mL) is from before the excursion, and no post-excursion titre is in the data. The potency loss is inferred from the pattern, not measured. Also, pd.material_lot still records LV25-118 at FRZ-80-02, even though DEV-26-021 says the contents were relocated to FRZ-80-01. That record needs checking.

**Weaker link: CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015 share the INC-03 door-alarm fault**

- **CAPA-26-012** comes from DEV-26-011. The recorded root cause is a misaligned INC-03 door switch, and the OQ door-open alarm took 142 s against a 60 s limit.
- **CAPA-26-015** comes from DEV-26-033. The recorded root cause is that the operator did not confirm the door latch, which is human error. INC-03's door was found not fully latched during PPQ26-02, and the door alarm was acknowledged about 10 hours after it started (21:40 to 07:50).
- Both events involve INC-03's door and alarm chain. The PPQ CAPA addresses only operator retraining, not the door-switch defect that CAPA-26-012 is meant to fix. I would treat this as a likely contributing cause rather than a proven one.

The other CAPA, CAPA-26-019 (DEV-26-041), is an independent supplier tubing defect and does not share a cause with the others.
